top.roles: persons, roles and groups (below: Entry in "roles"); the export lists them from the account down — whoever holds stands before what they hold
top.sealed: export only: how many roles can be seen in the account although this browser does not open them (they are not in the export); the import ignores this number

entryKey.id: role id from the export — an entry with "id" is a role that already exists and is changed in place; a new role has NO "id" (it gets one when created)
entryKey.key: a short name of the entry for "@key" references in this document — letters, digits, "-", "_", "." (up to 40 characters), e.g. "council"; "{account}" is reserved, "{self}" — only for your first person
entryKey.kind: "person" (a human being), "role" (a function someone fills and passes on) or "group" (those who belong to it); Polish works too: "osoba", "rola", "grupa". A new entry without "kind" is a "role". A role can be changed to a group and back, persons cannot
entryKey.name: name (up to {max} characters), sealed in the browser with the role's key — the service does not see it; for an entry with "id" a different name is a rename; a new role must have one
entryKey.holders: who holds this role (below: Who holds it); a new role is created by the first in the list who leads it ("holds" with signature) and whom you lead — the rest of the list is added afterwards
entryKey.areas: export information only: which areas the role leads to (itself or through roles it holds) — a list { "name", "level" } (below); the import does not change it, area access is granted in Areas
entryKey.link: export information only: true — this is the role of an access link; the import does not change it (neither the name, nor who holds it, nor what it holds) — links are changed at the links

areaKey.name: name of the area
areaKey.level: "read" (reads), "write" (writes) or "admin" (leads — can also let others in)

holderKey.by: who holds: "@key" (an entry of this document), "{self}" (your first person — the one from registration), "{account}" (the account; holds only persons) or a role "id" from the export. Instead of an object the string alone is enough — then "level": "holds" and "sign": true
holderKey.level: "holds" — leads: changes, passes on, admits others (default); "write" — writes: adds what belongs to the role; "read" — reads: sees. Polish works too: "prowadzi", "pisze", "czyta"
holderKey.sign: only with "holds": true (default) — also gets the signing key and acts on behalf of the role; false — belongs to the role without signature (as through a “Member” link). The import does not change the signature of an existing link

node.holderText:
{keys}
Whoever holds a role sees everything it sees (its areas, chats, calendars, the roles it holds); with the signing key they also act on its behalf. The same pair at another level is a separate link (e.g. "read" beside "holds"). The account holds only persons and only with "holds".
node.usage: How the app uses this data
node.usageText:
- The role graph is a graph of keys. Every link — also "write" and "read" — carries the role's key sealed for whoever holds it; the browser goes from the account downwards and opens as much as the links reach. The service has no keys — it only checks signatures.
- Access to an area (reads, writes, leads) is given to a role: the area's key and a certificate signed by the role that admits in the area. The certificate is valid for two years; after a year the browser of someone who admits in that area renews it by itself.
- The service lets into a role's areas only along "holds" (account → person → role → …, also through intermediate roles): those the role reaches this way see the chats, calendars and submissions of its areas, and news from them wakes their phones.
- A page address (and everything under it) is led by one role — the page is edited by those the role reaches along "holds".
- A form and an access link give their people a role; what it leads to is said by the role itself — one change applies to everyone who got it.
- The signing key ("sign": true, only with "holds") is acting on behalf of the role: it signs its messages in chats, the links in which it holds other roles (also new roles created under it), and the certificates it issues.
- A new "holds" therefore gives at once everything the role leads to — also through the roles it holds. The import does not grant access to areas or page addresses; a link is taken away by hand (Roles → role → “Take away”).
node.rootText:
The account's role structure: persons, roles and groups, who holds whom and at what level, with names. The account (the root) holds only persons; under the persons are roles and groups. Where: Roles → “More” (⋯) → “Import and export (JSON)” (#/workspace/roles).
What the import does:
- First it shows the list of changes with warnings; it saves only after “Import roles”.
- An entry with "id" (from the export) is a role that already exists: a different "name" renames it, "kind" "role" ↔ "group" changes the kind, new items in "holders" are added.
- An entry without "id" creates a new role or group — under the first item of "holders" that leads it ("holds" with signature) and that you lead with signature: your person ("{self}"), your role or another new role of this document ("@key" — that one is created first).
- Each new role is two RSA-4096 keys computed in the browser — a few seconds per role; at most {maxNew} new roles in one import (at most {maxEntries} entries in a document).
- It deletes nothing: roles, names and links that are not in the document stay; it does not change the signature of an existing link.
- It does not create accounts or persons (you create a person yourself: Roles → Account → “New person”); it does not touch roles this browser does not open, nor roles of access links ("link": true).
- It gives only what you can give: a role whose key you have (and with "sign": true — also its signing key), to someone on whose behalf you sign. What you cannot, it skips with a warning — likewise a link that would close a circle (two roles holding each other).
- Names are sealed in the browser with the role's key; the service only sees that the role exists and who holds it. The export file has the names in plain text — it is your copy.
Return ONE JSON object, without comments.

Document:
{top}

References in "by": "@key" — an entry of this document (also a new one); "{self}" — your first person; "{account}" — the account; or an "id" from the export.
